title: Latency bucketing failsafe and tenant-phased swap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a robust per-dependency/model/tenant circuit mechanism that triggers on latency tail behavior using an explicit latency-bucketing approach, and performs a phased tenant swap to safe fallbacks with minimal user-visible regressions.

Motivation: Current SLO-driven trips are either too coarse (per-service aggregate) or too sensitive (instant percentile spikes cause noisy trips). We need a middle ground that: 1) understands distributional shifts (not just single-point spikes), 2) adapts to tenant SLAs/tiering, and 3) performs safe, observable swap-to-fallback semantics (e.g., lighter quantized model / cached response / regional reroute).

Design summary:
- Latency bucketing: maintain a rolling histogram (10ms bins up to 2s, coarser above) per (tenant, model_variant, region, dependency). Compute percentile estimators (P50/P90/P99/P999) from buckets every 10s.
- Adaptive trip curve: instead of a binary threshold, compute a trip score using weighted percentiles: score = w1*norm(P99) + w2*norm(P999 spike factor) + w3*error_rate. Normalize to tenant SLA (higher-tier tenants have higher tolerance). Trip when score exceeds dynamic threshold for N consecutive windows (configurable, default N=3).
- Multi-region considerations: compute region-local scores; region-level trip can trigger local fallback first. Global pieces: if >50% of regions show sustained trips for the same dependency, escalate to cross-region failover to mirrored model endpoints in secondary region with warm cache prefill.
- Safe fallback choreography: staged steps with telemetry gates: 1) shadow reroute to fallback (no user traffic), 2) small-percentage traffic swap (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with realtime quality and cost checks, 3) full swap and degraded-mode indicators (add header/trace). Each step has automatic rollback conditions (quality drop > configured delta OR latency not improved within window).
- Load shedding and backpressure: for soft trips we prefer shed-by-priority: deprioritize background/low-cost requests, queue short requests (with bounded queue), and evict long-running ones. For hard trips we apply probabilistic shedding per-tenant according to budget.
- Observability & SLO linkage: every decision emits an event with the feature flags used, the percentile snapshot, and the chosen fallback path. Link events to SLO windows so on-call and PMs can correlate.

Trade-offs considered:
- Histogram buckets increase memory per key; mitigated by TTLing rarely used (low-traffic) tenant/model keys and falling back to coarse aggregates after inactivity.
- Staged swap is slower to mitigate bad fallbacks but reduces blast radius vs immediate full swap.
- Using weighted percentiles is more robust to localized jitter but needs tuning by tenant tier.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike (week 1): prototype bucketed rolling histogram lib (C++ runtime + telemetry export).
2) Simulation (week 2): run offline against 30 days of p99 traces from prod (grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/latency-buckets) to tune weights and N.
3) Canary (week 3): server-side small canary with 2 non-critical tenants, enable full staged swap logs + shadow reroute.
4) Rollout (week 4): enable for P3/P2 tenants, monitor.

Artifacts:
- Confluence runbook & design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Latency+Bucketing+Failsafe
- Spike PR (prototype histogram): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893
- Simulation notebook & results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-latency-sims
- Observability dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/latency-buckets-canary

Acceptance criteria:
- Bucketing lib runs with <2% overhead on CPU for median RPC path in canary.
- Trip decisions correlate with true user-impact windows in simulation (precision > 85% in detecting meaningful degradation).
- Rollout includes automated rollback and audit events; SLO alerts suppressed on safe fallbacks but surfaced in incident timeline.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives on noisy tenants: mitigate via tenant-specific historical baselines and minimum volume requirements before a trip can open.
- Memory growth: eviction policy + coarse fallback histogram.
- Bad fallback quality: every staged swap runs a lightweight quality regression check; if quality not acceptable, system reverts and flags for human review.

Next steps: finalize bucket sizes and weight defaults, complete simulation tuning, and schedule canary window with SRE team.
